newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond new issuance seen tapering off.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond new issuance seen tapering off.

text.p: Activity in the corporate bond primary sector is expected to taper off following a heavy week of issuance, which saw close to $4.0 billion in new investment-grade supply come to market, dealers said.
"Players are going to just sit back and digest this week's supply," said one high-grade syndicate source. "The tone so far in the market today has been very quiet."
Dealers said this week's bulk of high-grade supply was quickly absorbed and deals fared very well, including a number of global debt offerings, which served to boost this week's supply.
So far the only name to emerge for Friday's business is Suntrust Orlando's competitive bid offering for $100 million 10-year subordinated notes later this morning, players said.

Among global issues, the United Mexican States is expected to issue its US$1.0 billion global five-year debt offering via joint lead managers Hongkong Shanghai Bank and JP Morgan Securities, players said.
Still other names remain on the calendar for next week's business, dealers said.
RJR Nabisco is slated to issue $350 million in a two-part debt offering next week, syndicate players said.

The RJR deal is expected to include a $150 million seven-year issue and a $200 million 10-year issue, sources said. The offering will be jointly underwritten by Morgan Stanley & Co Inc and Merrill Lynch & Co, syndicate sources said.
In addition, Pohang Iron & Steel is expected to bring $300 million in 10-year debt via JP Morgan Securities Inc, players said.
Elsewhere, the high-yield sector may see some issues trickle in on Friday but overall a quiet day is on tap, players said.
Among the issues Equimar Shipholdings Ltd's will sell $100 million in 144A 10-year notes via Credit Suisse First Boston. Price talk on the issue is seen between 9.625 - 9.875 percent, sources said.

Also, Echostar DBS Corp will sell $325 million in five-year senior secured notes via Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette Securities, players said. Price talk on the issue is seen between 12.25 - 12.50 percent.

Seperately, Chase Telecommunications Inc's $160 million junk bond offering was indefinitely postponed late on Thursday as investors continued to turn a cold shoulder to startup telecom companies, according to a source close to the deal.
"It has been postponed due to difficulties in raising money for developmental (personal communication services)," the source said.
The deal failed to garner adequate investor interest even after it was restructured from units of zero coupon bonds with warrants to buy equity to a cash-paying, prefunded unit deal.

Price talk on the deal had initially called for senior discount notes with a 14 percent yield to maturity and 15 to 17 percent equity, then for 13-1/2 percent couponed seven-year senior notes and 20 percent equity, market sources said.

In Thursday's high-yield business, Hayes Wheels International sold $250 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes, rated B3/B, to yield 9.125 percent. CIBC Woody Gundy Securities Inc was the lead underwriter.
The bonds, which priced at par, are currently seen trading at 100-1/2 bid after weakening late Thursday to a 99-3/4 bid, players said.
Also on Thursday, Oxford Automotive sold $125 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes via Salomon Brothers Inc. The Caa1/B-minus bonds were priced at 99.851 to yield 10.125 percent.
Oxford's 10-year notes were seen trading higher in the secondary market at 100-3/4 bid, 101-3/4 offer, players said.
Next week's calendar continues to build with close to $1.7 billion in new high-yield supply expected to hit the market, players said.

Among the deals expected are: Belden & Blake Corp's $200 million issue, Brazos Sportswear's $100 million issue, DI Industries' $125 million offering, Indah Kiat Finance'S $500 million offering, Pierce Leahy's $100 million issue, Shoppers Food Warehouse'S $200 million issue, Talton Holdings $100 million issue, Telesystem International's $150 million offering, and West Coast Entertainment's $110 million issue, high-yield players said.
In the government market the benchmark U.S. Treasury bond is trading up 8/32 at 99-17/32 to yield 6.66 percent.
